title: Hardship tests conduct
meaning_odia: ଅଭାବର ଚାପରେ ମଣିଷର ସ୍ୱଭାବ ବା ଆଚରଣ ବିଗିଡ଼ିପାରେ ବୋଲି କଥାଟି କହେ। ଏହାକୁ ଏଠାରେ କଷ୍ଟର ପ୍ରଭାବ ନେଇ ଏକ ସତର୍କବାଣୀ ଭାବେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି, ଗରିବ ଲୋକଙ୍କ ଚରିତ୍ର ବିଷୟରେ ସାଧାରଣ ରାୟ ଭାବେ ନୁହେଁ।
explanation: The saying makes a stark link between deprivation and damaged conduct. This edition reads it as a warning that sustained hardship can strain patience and judgment. That interpretation concerns the pressure of circumstances; the proverb is not evidence that people with little money have worse character.
usage_example: In a story, someone who is usually patient begins speaking harshly under mounting shortages and worry. A reader might recall this saying when discussing that change. This is a newly composed illustration.
cultural_context: The sound echo between ଅଭାବ, want or lack, and ସ୍ୱଭାବ, disposition or habitual nature, gives the short line its force. Its categorical wording is preserved as the saying’s claim, while the commentary distinguishes that claim from a universal judgment about poverty.

witnesses.locator: Inspected public page line 122, ଅଭାବରୁ ସ୍ବଭାବ ନଷ୍ଟ.
witnesses.note: Uploaded PDF page 2 supplies the displayed short saying, without a missing-box glyph. Public Unicode transcription uses ସ୍ବଭାବ; display follows comparison transcription ସ୍ୱଭାବ. This is an orthographic transcription difference, not a different proverb. Shared source lineage is possible.

graphic.alt: A distressed adult holds his head beside nearly empty food jars and papers while another adult reaches toward him.
graphic.caption: An imagined moment of scarcity shows strain without making hardship a judgment of character.

odia_summary: ଅଭାବର ଚାପ ଆଚରଣକୁ ପ୍ରଭାବିତ କରିପାରେ ବୋଲି କଥାଟିର ସତର୍କବାଣୀ।
english_summary: The proverb warns of the strain that deprivation can place on conduct.
